presentingComplaint: Progressive headache, confusion and gait unsteadiness over 3 weeks
history: 78-year-old man brought by family with a 3-week history of gradually worsening dull global headache, increasing daytime drowsiness, word-finding difficulty and a subtle right-sided weakness noticed as tripping on the right foot. A minor fall backwards from standing height was recalled about 5 weeks ago with no loss of consciousness and no imaging at the time. Background of hypertension and atrial fibrillation for which he takes warfarin (self-reports variable INR monitoring). Independent at baseline; family report a personality change with apathy and fluctuating alertness rather than a sudden deficit.
examination: Alert but slow, GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6) with intermittent drowsiness. Mild expressive dysphasia and a subtle right pronator drift with brisk right-sided reflexes. No neck stiffness, no photophobia, no fever. Fundoscopy shows early blurring of disc margins. No external head wound; no petechiae or purpura. Gait unsteady and wide-based.
imaging: Non-contrast CT head: crescentic extra-axial collection over the left cerebral convexity, of mixed hypo-/iso-density (consistent with chronic-on-acute haematoma), with ~8 mm midline shift and effacement of the left lateral ventricle. No intraparenchymal haemorrhage or SAH.
finalDiagnosis: Chronic (chronic-on-acute) subdural haematoma with mass effect, on anticoagulation
citations: Harrison 22e - Concussion and Other Traumatic Brain Injuries / Cerebrovascular Diseases
Neurocritical Care Society / SCCM Reversal of Antithrombotics in Intracranial Hemorrhage 2016
contraindications: Supratherapeutic warfarin/INR - urgent reversal with 4-factor PCC plus IV vitamin K before or alongside neurosurgical intervention
Avoid resuming anticoagulation until bleeding controlled and neurosurgery consulted
Caution with sedatives given fluctuating GCS
edgeCases: Classic elderly-on-anticoagulant presentation with only trivial or forgotten head trauma
Fluctuating consciousness and cognitive decline can mimic dementia, delirium or 'stroke-like' TIA - a stroke mimic
Bilateral chronic SDH may cause minimal midline shift despite large volume, masking severity
expectedMaiK: In an elderly anticoagulated patient with a subacute, fluctuating headache, confusion and a lateralising deficit after a minor fall, a chronic subdural haematoma is the leading diagnosis - obtain an urgent non-contrast CT head, reverse the coagulopathy promptly, and involve neurosurgery. The supratherapeutic INR is a key driver of bleeding and must be corrected urgently.
expectedNextQuestions: Any history of head trauma or falls, even trivial, in the preceding weeks?
What anticoagulant/antiplatelet is he on and when was the last dose / most recent INR?
